scope: Strengthen the existing local modular foundation: transaction liveness/lifecycle hardening, REQ-003/005 revision 1 AC-1/AC-2 execution, explicit primitive/extension contracts and shared adapter checks. No new domain primitive, storage/wire migration, broad conformance, human validation or multi-user scale claim.

requirements.acceptance: AC-1: Reopen the same database with unchanged saved schema, fields and identities. AC-2: Opening an existing project does not reseed its contents.

criteria.method: Persist schema, entities, typed link, reusable resource, pinned reference, observation, receipt, successful command, named view, configuration and baseline. A separate CLI process exports the identical complete project. A fresh repository retains receipts, selected pins and original command outcome. Production UI confirmed title/statement edit survives server+database restart at both widths with identical saved schema/UUIDs/history/export.

Explicit --db plus --seed-demo rejects before changing that project. Existing-project CLI open, direct repository reopen and production server restart retain the complete export and allocate no new engineering records.

requirements.acceptance: AC-1: Valid confirmed edits persist and enter history. AC-2: An invalid or stale multi-operation change leaves every operation unapplied.

criteria.method: A create/entity-update/link-update batch commits exactly one project revision and three ordered immutable revisions with the expected UUIDs and versions. Confirmed production UI editing allocates one object revision and survives restart. Identical command replay returns the original result without another write.

A staged creation followed by an invalid field, stale entity, stale link or missing endpoint rejects without any difference in complete current/history/evidence export. Rejected commands reserve no success ID; a later valid command reuses the explicit object and command IDs. Shared adapter tests also verify rollback after low-level callback rejection and queue usability after nested-call rejection.

hardening.finding: A same-repository nested callback waits on the queue behind its own awaited outer callback.

before.boundedProbe: Disposable in-memory repository: still_pending, outerEntered=true at 100ms; queue dependency inspection identifies the wait cycle.

hardening.after: Reject before enqueue with a Tracer storage error; uncaught error rolls back the outer transaction. Independent callers still serialize; completed contexts do not lock later operations.

hardening.finding: Calling an already-closed repository leaks ERR_INVALID_STATE: database is not open.
hardening.after: Queue closure disables AsyncLocalStorage and rejects later calls with storage before callbacks execute. Queue checks closure again before starting accepted work. Callers still drain pending work before closing; no new cancellation guarantee is claimed.

architecture.layers: Domain and application remain platform-independent; persistence owns Node async context and driver lifetime. Existing typed commands/queries, identities, revisions, resources, references and receipts remain authoritative.
architecture.scalingLimits: SQLite still serializes repository transactions and uses BEGIN IMMEDIATE, including reads. This fixes liveness/lifetime faults; it does not remove lock contention or prove a team backend. Select indexed/paged workloads and prove adapter snapshot/concurrency/history/evidence parity before another backend is supported.

focused.scope: Shared SQLite adapter contract, durability criteria and server shutdown draining.
